questions.solution_html:
• Define and give the importance of Kiliani-Fischer synthesis [U] / [CO1]
  • The Kiliani-Fischer synthesis is a method used to lengthen the carbon chain of aldoses
  • (sugars) by adding one carbon atom. It involves reacting an aldose with hydrogen cyanide
  • (HCN) to form a cyanohydrin, which is then reduced to an aldehyde and hydrolyzed to
  • yield the longer chain aldose. This process creates two epimers (diastereomers) at the
  • new stereogenic center.

questions.question: Make a detailed note on the following a. Mutarotation b. Optical Isomerism c. D and L Isomers d. Chirality and 2n rule / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Make a detailed note on the following [U] / [CO1]
  • (1 marks each )
  • a. Mutarotation - Mutarotation is the change in optical rotation of a solution of a cyclic sugar
  • (like glucose) due to the interconversion of its anomeric forms (alpha and beta) when dissolved
  • in water. This phenomenon occurs because the alpha and beta anomers interconvert until they
  • reach an equilibrium.
  • b. OpticalIsomerism -Optical isomerism, a type of stereoisomerism, refers to the phenomenon
  • where molecules with the same mol ecular formula and bond arrangement have different spatial
  • arrangements of atoms, resulting in non -superimposable mirror images. These mirror images,
  • called enantiomers, have the same physical properties but differ in their interaction with plane -
  • polarized light.
  • c. D and L Isomers - D and L isomers, also known as enantiomers, are mirror-image
  • stereoisomers that differ in the arrangement of their chiral carbons. The "D" and "L"
  • designations, derived from Latin ("dexter" and "laevus" meaning right and left) , indicate the
  • configuration of the most chiral carbon in a molecule, specifically in carbohydrates and amino
  • acids.
  • d. Chirality and 2 n -chirality refers to molecules that are non-superimposable mirror images of
  • each other. For a molecule with 'n' chir al centers, the maximum number of possible
  • stereoisomers (including enantiomers and diastereomers) is 2n.

• Evaluate the structure, properties and functions of major phospholipids.
  • [A]/[CO4]
  • Phospholipids are amphipathic lipids containing glycerol, fatty acids, phosphate and
  • nitrogenous base
  • Major phospholipids
  • Phosphatidylcholine (lecithin)
  • Phosphatidylethanolamine
  • Phosphatidylserine
  • Sphingomyelin
  • Properties
  • Amphipathic nature with hydrophilic and hydrophobic regions
  • Form bilayers in aqueous systems
  • Act as emulsifying agents
  • Functions
  • Major structural components of cell membranes
  • Involved in membrane fluidity and permeability
  • Function in lipid transport and signaling
  • Important in nerve tissue and lipoprotein structure
